subject: Civil Rights Complaint Against Medford Police
overview: Host Danielle Balocca and Human Rights Commission Chair Chelli Keshavan interview attorney Sophia Hall about a civil rights complaint filed against the Medford Police Department regarding a July 2021 traffic stop involving two Black college students.

items.title: Introduction and Juneteenth Observance
items.summary: Danielle Balocca introduces the episode on Juneteenth, framing the history of Emancipation alongside the legal and lived experiences of freedom across races.

items.title: July 2021 Police Stop Allegations
items.summary: Sophia Hall recounts the July 2021 incident in which two Black Medford High School graduates were stopped near High Street, held at gunpoint, handcuffed, and searched by Medford police officers without explanation before being released.

items.title: Demands for Restitution and Policy Reform
items.summary: Hall details the complaint's requests for an apology, compensation for emotional distress, external expert review of department policies, and mandatory, recurring implicit bias training.

items.title: Police Oversight and Community Engagement
items.summary: The discussion covers limitations of internal affairs self-policing, statewide accountability efforts under the POST Commission, and avenues for resident engagement through the city council and diversity office.
